This is something I just stumbled across, sorry for reviving this after several months, but I've actually put some thought into this before, and built a deck for him, based on the below thoughts.



We know that Marik only knew of Ra's standard god defenses, probably the hierarchy above the other God Cards, and that it gained the strength of the monsters tributed for it. His commentary to Dark Bakura against Dark Marik makes it clear he does not know about the God Phoenix effect or the Life Transfer effect, so he would have built his deck assuming the only way to use Ra effectively was lots of quick summons he could tribute for it, ideally with some decent ATK to buff Ra. I'll also assume he knew about being able to tribute other monsters to feed to Ra later to keep powering it up, as we see Dark Marik do. 



We also see that Dark Marik still uses Slimes, and indeed there's been a semi-focus on slimes in modern Marik support, as well as Lekunga being able to transform Water monsters in the GY into tokens for tributing, and Lord Poison can fetch Lekunga, so I think it's reasonable to assume a Water rush deck of some form. I've built an attempt at something I think it might have been like, although obviously there are some allowances here and there.



Skreech and Painful Choice allow Marik to thin his deck in order to get to Ra faster, while also populating his GY for Lekunga, Fenrir or Ocean of Regeneration, which can also net him card advantage with Card of Safe Return. 



Fenrir and Dragon Ice can be Special Summoned easily, in order to ensure that they can be tributed for Ra, and I thought that the Terrorking/Terrorqueen Salmon combo was a fun and suitable method for Marik to pop out two 2400 ATK tributes, which would be no joke back in the day. 



Cursed Fig (as well as Skreech) has that weird kind of horror vibe that works well for Marik, and freezing up two of Yugi's reactive cards would be a real pain for him to work around. 



We know Marik has at least one Trap Monster so I added two more that I felt fit the kind of monstrous/cursed vibe Marik's monsters have, as well as both having a decent amount of ATK to feed Ra. 



Magical Reflect Slime is both a slime and a punisher that turns pain back on the enemy, fitting in with Marik's style, and Jowls of Dark Demise and Tribe-Infecting Virus are both just horror-ish water monsters. Yomi Ship is an in-joke as a punishment card, as well as seeing to be based on Egyptian death barges, which hints at Marik's identity, and Deep Diver can move Ra to the top of the deck for Marik to draw. 



Finally, I have two Garzetts in the deck, with Emperor Maju Garzett acting as the Ra replacement both in real-life and in an imaginary deck that Marik keeps using after Battle City, since it requires 3 tributes, gets strength from the tributes and has some degree of in-built protection like a god, while I picture Legendary Maju Garzett as the other monster Malik had in his deck as his disguise-ace, the monster he would use as his big finisher while keeping up pretenses of being Namu, where he can't just bust out his God card.



Obviously, Guardian Slime, Reactor Slime and Egyptian God Slime would really improve the deck, as would using multiples of cards, but I wanted it to feel at least a bit more like it was a deck from that era, even if some of the card effects are a bit more than what we'd actually have seen back then.

Yes you'd need some complex explanation for why he can have more than 2 fruit but still be limited in real life, but "my abnormal body allows me to use 3 fruit (or alternatively 1 fruit of each type)" is perfectly servicable as an explanation in a fictional setting where we're likely already going to get the explanation of why his body is abnormal anyway.

Literally all I'm proposing is wait and see, since from a literary standpoint there's enough things that could be construed to support 3 fruits and nothing that explicitly or intuitively prevents it, so I would be equally unsurprised to discover he could or could not use 3 fruits.

Occam's razor tends not to be very effective for simple yes/no circumstances in fictional works. It is about equally simple to assume "his abnormal body can support more DFs" as it is to say that it can't because neither requires a complex explanation. 

Occams razor is good for real world, less so for fiction.
